🔍 Search Terms

content mapper, contentMappers, moduleSuffixes, platform suffix, platform variants, custom file extension, extraExtensions, React Native, .web, .ios

 ✅ Viability Checklist

- [x] This wouldn't be a breaking change in existing TypeScript/JavaScript code
- [x] This wouldn't change the runtime behavior of existing JavaScript code
- [x] This could be implemented without emitting different JS based on the types of the expressions
- [x] This isn't a runtime feature (e.g. library functionality, non-ECMAScript syntax with JavaScript output, new syntax sugar for JS, etc.)
- [x] This isn't a request to add a new utility type: 
- [x] This feature would agree with the rest of our Design Goals: 

 ⭐ Suggestion

An optional moduleSuffixes array on a contentMappers entry:

 

For files with that entry's extensions, the entry's list is used instead of the moduleSuffixes compiler option, and each suffix goes in front of the extension, the way the compiler option already places it for .ts, .tsx, .mts, .cts and .json:

 

What stays the same:

- Imports still name the mapped extension. Nothing is implied: ./card stays unresolved.
- An entry without moduleSuffixes resolves exactly as today, including the compiler option's placement after the extension (64548).
- The compiler option keeps applying to .ts and every other built-in extension, whatever the entry says.
- The mapper process takes no part in resolution. The list comes from the project's tsconfig, not from the mapper package.
- Today the key is ignored without an error, so no existing config depends on it.

Because the entry has its own list, the compiler option doesn't have to serve two purposes: a project can pick .ios variants of its .ts files and .web variants of its mapped files, or suffix only one of the two.

 📃 Motivating Example

Platform variants in React Native-style projects: Card.web.tsrx and Card.ios.tsrx next to Card.tsrx, one per platform build. With the compiler option, TypeScript picks target.web.ts for ./target.ts, but it cannot pick card.web.foo for ./card.foo: the suffix is added after the whole file name (64548). If a file with that name exists, the import resolves to it and fails:

 

So for mapped files the compiler option cannot select a variant today. The entry option gives them their own list without changing what the compiler option does.

 Prototype and results

A prototype against main at b85298b: 7 files, +53/−3 (diff below). Results with the identity .foo mapper from 64546's reproduction, tsc --runExternalCode --traceResolution, main vs. a local build of main with the prototype:

| Setup | Import | main | prototype |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| entry [".web", ""], card.foo and card.web.foo | ./card.foo | card.foo | card.web.foo |
| entry [".web", ""], only card.foo | ./card.foo | card.foo | card.foo |
| entry [".web", ""], imported from another .foo file | ./card.foo | card.foo | card.web.foo |
| entry [".web", ""], no compiler option, target.ts and target.web.ts | ./target.ts | target.ts | target.ts |
| compiler option [".ios", ""] and entry [".web", ""] | ./target.ts | target.ios.ts | target.ios.ts |
| compiler option [".ios", ""] and entry [".web", ""], card.ios.foo and card.web.foo | ./card.foo | card.foo (tries card.foo.ios) | card.web.foo |
| entry without moduleSuffixes, compiler option [".web", ""] | ./card.foo | card.foo (tries card.foo.web) | same |
| entry [], compiler option [".web", ""], card.foo.web exists | ./card.foo | card.foo.web, TS6054 and TS7016 | card.foo |
| entry [".web"] (no ""), only card.foo | ./card.foo | card.foo | TS2307, as with the compiler option |
| entry "moduleSuffixes": ".web" | | ignored | TS5024: contentMapper.moduleSuffixes requires a value of type string[] |

- An --incremental rebuild after changing the entry's list resolves again with the new list (checked [".web", ""] → [""] → [".web", ""]).
- go test ./internal/module/... ./internal/modulespecifiers/... ./internal/contentmapper/... ./internal/compiler/... ./internal/project/... and the content-mapper tests in ./internal/tsoptions pass. I ran them from a sparse clone without testdata, so tests that compare against reference baselines were left out (two in internal/project, the rest of internal/tsoptions).
- Not covered: the API's module-resolution request (internal/api/module_resolution.go) builds its resolver from the snapshot's extension list and would need the same map. I have not checked the editor.

 Relation to 64549

64549 suggests extensionless lookup for registered extensions. The two are independent. With both, ./card resolves to card.web.foo when the entry sets [".web", ""]. With 64549 alone, ./card resolves to card.foo even when the compiler option is [".web", ""], because the suffix still lands after .foo. Both were checked with local builds of each combination.

 💻 Use Cases

1. What do you want to use this for? TSRX type-checks .tsrx files through a content mapper on TypeScript 7 (tsrx-org/tsrx135). Cross-platform projects keep per-platform component files (Card.web.tsrx, Card.ios.tsrx), and the checker should pick the same variant the platform build uses.
2. What shortcomings exist with current approaches? The compiler option's placement is intended (64548), so it cannot select variants of mapped files, and changing it would change resolution for every project. A mapper cannot help: it is asked for a file's content after resolution has picked the file.
3. What workarounds are you using in the meantime? One .ts re-export per variant (card.web.ts re-exporting ./card.web.foo) so the compiler option has a built-in extension to work with, or generated .d.ts re-exports in a hidden folder merged in with rootDirs. Both add a file per variant that has to be kept in sync with the file system.

 
 Prototype diff (whitespace-only gofmt realignment left out) 

 

 

The prototype and results were prepared with Claude Code; every result above was run locally.

🔍 Search Terms

content mapper, built-in extension, dynamic LSP registration, duplicate inlay hints

 ✅ Viability Checklist

- [x] This wouldn't be a breaking change in existing TypeScript/JavaScript code
- [x] This wouldn't change the runtime behavior of existing JavaScript code
- [x] This could be implemented without emitting different JS based on the types of the expressions
- [x] This isn't a runtime feature (e.g. library functionality, non-ECMAScript syntax with JavaScript output, new syntax sugar for JS, etc.)
- [x] This isn't a request to add a new utility type: 
- [x] This feature would agree with the rest of our Design Goals: 

 ⭐ Suggestion

Content Mappers currently target otherwise unsupported file extensions. It would be useful to let a mapper explicitly opt in to transforming files with built-in TypeScript/JavaScript extensions, such as .ts, while keeping the current restriction as the default.

The feature should also define how mapper applicability is scoped. For example, a mapper could explicitly claim selected .ts files, or be responsible for returning an unchanged, correctly mapped result when a file contains no syntax it handles. Simply registering .ts globally could otherwise cause ordinary TypeScript files to be transformed unexpectedly.

When a built-in extension is enabled, LSP capabilities already provided for JavaScript/TypeScript documents should not be registered again for the same documents. This is important for avoiding duplicate language-feature results, such as inlay hints.

 📃 Motivating Example

I’m building a tool that adds Result/Option-style early-return syntax to TypeScript. For example, it could transform:

 

into virtual TypeScript such as:

 

The tool can generate valid TypeScript and mappings back to the original source, but it cannot use Content Mapper for this workflow because the input file is .ts, a built-in extension.

 💻 Use Cases

- User-defined syntax sugar or macro-like transforms within ordinary .ts files.
- Result/Option workflows that unwrap values and propagate failures.
- Other source-level transforms that produce valid virtual TypeScript while retaining useful source mappings for language-service features.

The goal is not to add Result/Option semantics to TypeScript itself. It is to let users opt into their own transformation while keeping ordinary TypeScript behavior unchanged unless explicitly configured.
kept_issues.title: Feature Request: Allow Content Mappers to opt-in to transforming files end in built-in extensions
